## 15) Plots of change in outcomes due to increasing test sensitivity

For every outcome plotted in section [14) Plots of outcomes by daily probability of testing and test sensitivity], the change from increasing test sensitivity from `sens_from` to `sens_to` (set in section [14) Plots of outcomes by daily probability of testing and test sensitivity]; both must be values in the grid), reported separately for each isolation policy (P1, P2 and P3), at the same daily probability of testing:

> avoided = value at `sens_from` − value at `sens_to` (counts per year avoided, and reductions in the other outcomes, e.g. discharge prevalence, length of stay, specimens tested per confirmed case and mean times to testing and treatment; a negative value is an increase)
>
> additional = value at `sens_to` − value at `sens_from`, for outcomes that rise as more cases are confirmed (confirmed and recovered cases, side-room bed-days and their share of all bed-days; a negative value is a decrease)
>
> change in the shares of CDI cases tested (Outcome A3, Outcome A4) and confirmed (Outcome A5, Outcome A6) = value at `sens_to` − value at `sens_from`, in percentage points

The changes in total CDI cases (Outcome A1) and hospital-acquired CDI cases (Outcome B2) are identical (see the note in section [14) Plots of outcomes by daily probability of testing and test sensitivity]). Sensitivity does not change who is sent for testing, so Outcome A3 and the mean time to first test (Outcome D5) do not change. The outcomes reported are set by the `gain` column of `grid_outcome_spec`, and how each is reported by its `direction` column, in `Scripts/Model4_Functions.R`. Each tab shows a table and a chart. The table has one row per isolation policy and daily probability of testing (`r paste(fmt_prob(gain_table_sent), collapse = " and ")`, `gain_table_sent`), ordered by policy, with the values at `sens_from` and `sens_to`, the change between them, and the arc elasticity of the outcome with respect to test sensitivity, calculated by the midpoint method:

> arc elasticity = (change in outcome / midpoint of outcome) / (change in sensitivity / midpoint of sensitivity)

This is the % change in the outcome for a 1% change in test sensitivity, over the step from `r pc(sens_from)` to `r pc(sens_to)` (midpoint `r pc((sens_from + sens_to) / 2)`). It uses the actual change in the outcome, so it is negative where the outcome falls as sensitivity rises (whether that change is reported as "avoided" or not). An elasticity below -1 or above 1 means the outcome responds more than in proportion to sensitivity. It is not shown ("-") where the outcome's midpoint is 0 (e.g. side-room bed-days under P1), or for the differences in prevalence between discharge and admission (Outcome B3), which can be negative or close to 0, so a % change is not meaningful. The elasticities are also saved in `sensitivity_gain_<from>_to_<to>.csv`.

The chart shows the outcome itself (not the change) at both sensitivities, for every daily probability of testing in the grid:

- one panel per isolation policy, with the same y axis so the panels are comparable;
- dashed lines at `sens_from` and solid lines at `sens_to`; the shaded band between them is the change;
- a dotted grey line for the value with no testing (0%, the same under every policy);
- on the x axis, the daily probability of testing (`prob_test_daily`) on a log scale from 0.01 (each doubling takes the same width, so the low values, where outcomes change fastest, keep room; testing increases from left to right); no testing (0.00) cannot be shown on a log scale, so it is the dotted horizontal line.

This shows each change against the level it starts from, so a policy with more of an outcome does not necessarily gain the most. The testing outputs that follow from each `prob_test_daily` (as in section [13) Table of research question outcomes]; they are also plotted in sections [14) Plots of outcomes by daily probability of testing and test sensitivity] and [15) Plots of change in outcomes due to increasing test sensitivity]: the shares of incident (Outcome A3) and prevalent (Outcome A4) CDI cases ever tested, and the mean times to first test (Outcome D5) and to treatment (Outcome D6)) are:

```{r}

  format_testing_outputs(testing_outputs),
  caption = paste0("Testing outputs by daily probability of testing, at ",
                   scales::percent(testing_outputs_sens), " test sensitivity (Outcome A4: prevalent CDI cases ever ",
                   "tested at model stabilisation, by isolation policy)")
)
```

With no testing nobody is tested, so nothing changes. All values are saved as `sensitivity_gain_<from>_to_<to>.csv`.

## 16) Commentary on the effect of improving test sensitivity

```{r}
#| label: gain-note-values
#| include: false
# Figures for the commentary: values and changes from sens_from to sens_to at the daily probabilities
# of testing in gain_table_sent (counts per year)
lo_sent <- min(gain_table_sent)
hi_sent <- max(gain_table_sent)
# Value at sens_from or sens_to, or the change as reported in section 15 (avoided, additional or change)
sg <- function(var, pol, sent, col) {
  sensitivity_gain[[col]][sensitivity_gain$outcome == var & sensitivity_gain$isolation_policy == pol &
                            abs(sensitivity_gain$prob_test_daily - sent) < 1e-6]
}
gain <- function(var, pol, sent = hi_sent) sg(var, pol, sent, "gain")
v_from <- function(var, pol, sent = hi_sent) sg(var, pol, sent, "value_from")
v_to   <- function(var, pol, sent = hi_sent) sg(var, pol, sent, "value_to")
# Change from sens_from to sens_to in a final outcome column not in the section 15 outcomes (per year)
chg <- function(var, pol, sent = hi_sent) gval(var, pol, sent, sens_to) - gval(var, pol, sent, sens_from)
# Formats: counts, percentages, percentage-point changes and days
prop <- function(x) scales::percent(x, accuracy = 0.1)   # proportions and shares
ppc <- function(x) paste0(sprintf("%+.1f", 100 * x), " pp")
d1  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
d2  <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
# "P1 a, P2 b, P3 c" for one outcome, using value function f and format fmt
trio <- function(var, sent = hi_sent, f = gain, fmt = n0) {
  paste0("P1 ", fmt(f(var, P1, sent)), ", P2 ", fmt(f(var, P2, sent)), ", P3 ", fmt(f(var, P3, sent)))
}
# Policies ordered by the change (largest first), e.g. "P2, then P3, then P1"
gain_order <- function(var, sent = hi_sent) {
  pols <- c(P1 = P1, P2 = P2, P3 = P3)
  g <- vapply(pols, \(p) gain(var, p, sent), numeric(1))
  paste(names(sort(g, decreasing = TRUE)), collapse = ", then ")
}
# "rises" or "falls" for a change (value at sens_to minus value at sens_from)
dir_word <- function(x) if (x >= 0) "rises" else "falls"
# Arc elasticity (midpoint method) of one outcome under one policy, and formatted for three policies
el   <- function(var, pol, sent = hi_sent) sg(var, pol, sent, "elasticity")
e2   <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
etri <- function(var, sent = hi_sent) trio(var, sent, el, e2)
# Outcomes grouped by responsiveness at one daily probability of testing, using the largest absolute
# elasticity across the three policies: "elastic" (>= 1), "responsive" (>= 0.1 and < 1) or "barely"
# (< 0.1). Returns their labels (without the "Outcome A1: " text), joined with semicolons.
el_group <- function(group, sent = hi_sent) {
  spec <- grid_outcome_spec |> filter(gain)
  max_abs <- vapply(spec$variable, \(v) {
    x <- abs(vapply(c(P1, P2, P3), \(p) el(v, p, sent), numeric(1)))
    if (all(is.na(x))) NA_real_ else max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
  keep <- switch(group,
    elastic    = !is.na(max_abs) & max_abs >= 1 - 1e-9,
    responsive = !is.na(max_abs) & max_abs >= 0.1 & max_abs < 1 - 1e-9,
    barely     = !is.na(max_abs) & max_abs < 0.1)
  labs <- sub("^Outcome ([A-D]\\d+): (.*)$", "\\2 (Outcome \\1)", spec$label[keep])
  if (length(labs) == 0) "none" else paste(lower_first(labs), collapse = "; ")
}
# Policies ordered by absolute elasticity (most responsive first), e.g. "P2, then P3, then P1"
el_order <- function(var, sent = hi_sent) {
  e <- abs(c(P1 = el(var, P1, sent), P2 = el(var, P2, sent), P3 = el(var, P3, sent)))
  paste(names(sort(e, decreasing = TRUE)), collapse = ", then ")
}
```

This section summarises the plots and tables in section [15) Plots of change in outcomes due to increasing test sensitivity], by research question. The figures are per year (counts) for an increase in test sensitivity from `r pc(sens_from)` to `r pc(sens_to)`, at a daily probability of testing of `r prob(lo_sent)` and `r prob(hi_sent)` (`gain_table_sent`, as in the section [15) Plots of change in outcomes due to increasing test sensitivity] tables), and are calculated from the scenario grid, so they stay correct if parameters change.

Better sensitivity helps mostly by giving fewer false negative results: fewer patients cycle between awaiting a result (Xtest) and false negatives on the ward (FN), and more are confirmed and treated sooner. The share of results that are positive equals the test sensitivity under every policy, so it rises by the same amount (`r prop(pos_share(P1, sens_from))` to `r prop(pos_share(P1, sens_to))`) under each; the differences between policies come from where each group of patients is cared for.

**A) Case ascertainment**

- **Incident CDI cases (Outcome A1)**: the cases avoided are all hospital-acquired, so they equal Outcome B2 (see B) Transmission below).
- **Missed CDI cases (Outcome A2)**: `r trio("cum_total_missed_cases")` avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)` (most under `r gain_order("cum_total_missed_cases")`), and `r trio("cum_total_missed_cases", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`. They are almost all false negatives discharged or dying in FN, T4 or T3 (change at `r prob(hi_sent)`: `r trio("cum_missed_false_negative_cases", hi_sent, chg, n0p)`); missed untested cases (from I) barely change, as sensitivity does not affect who is tested. The amounts avoided broadly follow the number of false negatives at risk at `r pc(sens_from)` sensitivity (`r trio("cum_missed_false_negative_cases", hi_sent, \(v, p, s) gval(v, p, s, sens_from))` per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`).
- **CDI cases ever tested (Outcome A3, Outcome A4)**: sensitivity does not change who is sent for testing, so the share of incident cases ever sent for testing (Outcome A3) is unchanged (`r prop(v_from("prop_sent_for_testing", P1, lo_sent))` at `r prob(lo_sent)` and `r prop(v_from("prop_sent_for_testing", P1, hi_sent))` at `r prob(hi_sent)`). The point-prevalence share ever tested (Outcome A4) `r dir_word(gain("prop_current_CDI_tested", P1))` slightly (`r trio("prop_current_CDI_tested", hi_sent, gain, ppc)` at `r prob(hi_sent)`), as fewer tested patients stay in hospital as false negatives waiting to be retested.
- **CDI cases confirmed (Outcome A5)**: the share of incident cases confirmed rises from `r prop(v_from("prop_confirmed", P1))` to `r prop(v_to("prop_confirmed", P1))` under P1 at `r prob(hi_sent)` (`r prop(v_from("prop_confirmed", P1, lo_sent))` to `r prop(v_to("prop_confirmed", P1, lo_sent))` at `r prob(lo_sent)`), with similar values under P2 and P3: `r trio("cum_confirmed_cases")` additional confirmed cases per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`.
- **Confirmed via retest (Outcome A6)**: falls (`r trio("cum_confirmed_via_retest", hi_sent, gain, n0p)` per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`), as fewer cases have a false negative result first.

**B) Transmission**

- **Hospital-acquired colonisations (Outcome B1)**: `r trio("cum_colonised_in_hospital")` avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)` (most under `r gain_order("cum_colonised_in_hospital")`), and `r trio("cum_colonised_in_hospital", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`.
- **Hospital-acquired CDI cases (Outcome B2)**: `r trio("cum_hospital_attributable_I")` avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)` (most under `r gain_order("cum_hospital_attributable_I")`), and `r trio("cum_hospital_attributable_I", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)` (most under `r gain_order("cum_hospital_attributable_I", lo_sent)`). They follow the hospital-acquired colonisations avoided (Outcome B1). At `r prob(hi_sent)`:
  - *P2*: suspected cases wait for their result on a general ward, so fewer retests mean fewer days in Xtest on the ward (colonisations from Xtest `r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_Xtest", P2))`) and as FN (`r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_FN", P2))`). The extra confirmed cases are isolated after a short wait on the ward (T1), so they add little transmission (colonisations from Xtreat `r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_Xtreat", P2))`, from T1 `r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_T1", P2))`).
  - *P1* gains as much as P2 from fewer days in Xtest (`r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_Xtest", P1))`) and as FN (`r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_FN", P1))`), but the extra confirmed cases are treated on a general ward and transmit at `betaXtreat`, adding `r n0(chg("cum_colonised_from_Xtreat", P1))` colonisations from Xtreat and offsetting much of the gain.
  - *P3*: suspected cases are already isolated, so less time in Xtest saves little (`r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_Xtest", P3))`), and the gain comes mainly from fewer days as FN (`r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_FN", P3))`) and waiting on the ward for a side room before retesting (T3, `r n0p(chg("cum_colonised_from_T3", P3))`). P3 also starts from fewer cases (`r trio("cum_hospital_attributable_I", hi_sent, v_from)` hospital-acquired CDI cases per year at `r pc(sens_from)` sensitivity).
- **Prevalence at discharge (Outcome B3)**: CDI prevalence at discharge falls (`r trio("prop_discharged_CDI", hi_sent, gain, \(x) ppc(-x))` at `r prob(hi_sent)`, from `r prop(v_from("prop_discharged_CDI", P1))` to `r prop(v_to("prop_discharged_CDI", P1))` under P1; `r trio("prop_discharged_CDI", lo_sent, gain, \(x) ppc(-x))` at `r prob(lo_sent)`), as fewer false negatives are discharged untreated. Colonisation prevalence at discharge falls by less (`r trio("prop_discharged_C", hi_sent, gain, \(x) ppc(-x))` at `r prob(hi_sent)`), following the reduction in hospital-acquired colonisation. Admission prevalence is fixed, so the differences between discharge and admission prevalence change by the same amounts.

**C) Hospital resource use**

- **Patient bed-days and length of stay (Outcome C1)**: change little (`r trio("hospital_bed_days")` bed-days avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`; average length of stay `r d2(v_from("avg_LOS", P1))` days under P1, shortened by `r trio("avg_LOS", hi_sent, gain, \(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3))` days), mainly because fewer patients spend extra days awaiting retest results (there is no discharge from Xtest).
- **General ward and side-room bed-days (Outcome C2 to Outcome C4)**: there are no side rooms under P1. Under P2 and P3 more confirmed cases are isolated, so side-room bed-days rise (P2 `r n0p(gain("side_room_bed_days", P2))`, P3 `r n0p(gain("side_room_bed_days", P3))` per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`; share of all bed-days `r prop(v_from("prop_side_room_bed_days", P2))` to `r prop(v_to("prop_side_room_bed_days", P2))` under P2 and `r prop(v_from("prop_side_room_bed_days", P3))` to `r prop(v_to("prop_side_room_bed_days", P3))` under P3), and general ward bed-days fall (`r trio("general_ward_bed_days")` avoided). `r if (gain("side_room_bed_days", P3) < gain("side_room_bed_days", P2)) "The rise is smaller under P3, as suspected cases are already in a side room while awaiting their result." else ""`
- **Faecal specimens tested (Outcome C5, Outcome C6)**: `r trio("cum_total_test")` tests avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)` (`r trio("cum_total_test", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`), as fewer false negatives are retested. Specimens tested per confirmed case fall from `r d2(v_from("tests_per_confirmed", P1))` to `r d2(v_to("tests_per_confirmed", P1))` under every policy and daily probability of testing: each test is positive with probability equal to the sensitivity, so this is 1 / sensitivity.

**D) CDI case outcomes**

- **Treated and recovered (Outcome D1) and discharged untreated (Outcome D2)**: treated and recovered cases rise with the cases confirmed (`r trio("cum_recovered_cases", hi_sent, gain, n0p)` per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`), and cases discharged untreated fall (`r trio("cum_discharges_while_infected")` avoided), as fewer false negatives are discharged before a retest.
- **Deaths (Outcome D3, Outcome D4)**: change little, as the death rate is low (deaths following CDI `r trio("cum_deaths_post_infection", hi_sent, gain, d1)` avoided per year at `r prob(hi_sent)`, of which CDI-attributable `r trio("cum_deaths_CDI_attributable", hi_sent, gain, d1)`).
- **Mean times to first test and to treatment (Outcome D5, Outcome D6)**: the time to first test does not change (`r d1(v_from("mean_wait_test", P1))` days under P1 and P2 and `r d1(v_from("mean_wait_test", P3))` under P3 at `r prob(hi_sent)`). The time to treatment is shortened by `r trio("mean_wait_treatment", hi_sent, gain, d1)` days at `r prob(hi_sent)`, and by the same amount at `r prob(lo_sent)` (`r trio("mean_wait_treatment", lo_sent, gain, d1)`): the delay from false negative results and retests does not depend on how quickly the first test is taken. Under P3 each retest also waits for a side room (T3), so the saving is larger.

**In short**, improving sensitivity avoids most hospital-acquired CDI under `r gain_order("cum_hospital_attributable_I")` at `r prob(hi_sent)` (`r gain_order("cum_hospital_attributable_I", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`): it matters most where suspected cases wait on a general ward and confirmed cases are isolated (P2). Where suspected cases are already isolated (P3), isolation already prevents much of the transmission that better sensitivity would avoid; where confirmed cases stay on a general ward (P1), the extra confirmed cases offset much of the gain. Across all policies, better sensitivity confirms more cases, misses fewer, uses fewer tests and shortens the time to treatment, and most of these gains are larger the more cases are sent for testing.

## 17) Responsiveness of outcomes to improving test sensitivity

The arc elasticity in the section [15) Plots of change in outcomes due to increasing test sensitivity] tables is the % change in an outcome for a 1% improvement in test sensitivity, over the step from `r pc(sens_from)` to `r pc(sens_to)` (midpoint `r pc((sens_from + sens_to) / 2)`), calculated by the midpoint method. A negative elasticity means the outcome falls as sensitivity improves; an absolute value of 1 or more means the outcome responds more than in proportion to sensitivity.

The chart below compares the elasticities of all outcomes, in outcome label order, at daily probabilities of testing of `r prob(lo_sent)` and `r prob(hi_sent)`. Each point is one isolation policy; outcomes beyond the dashed lines (-1 and +1) respond more than in proportion to sensitivity. The Outcome B3 differences in prevalence have no elasticity (a % change is not meaningful for a difference that can be 0 or negative), and side-room bed-days have none under P1 (there are no side rooms).

```{r}
#| label: elasticity-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9.45
#| fig-height: 9.06
#| out-width: 100%
# Arc elasticities of every outcome (from sensitivity_gain, section 15) at the daily probabilities of
# testing in gain_table_sent; helpers el(), etri(), el_group() and el_order() are in section 16
elasticity_plot <- plot_elasticities(sensitivity_gain, sens_from, sens_to, sent = gain_table_sent)
ggsave(file.path(output_dir, sprintf("sensitivity_elasticity_%03d_to_%03d.png",
                                     round(100 * sens_from), round(100 * sens_to))),
       elasticity_plot, width = 24, height = 23, dpi = 300, units = "cm")
elasticity_plot
```

Grouping the outcomes by the largest absolute elasticity across the three policies, at a daily probability of testing of `r prob(hi_sent)`:

- **More than in proportion (1 or more)**: `r el_group("elastic")`.
  - Cases confirmed via retest (Outcome A6) fall fastest (`r etri("cum_confirmed_via_retest")`), as better sensitivity leaves fewer false negative results to be retested.
  - Missed cases (Outcome A2), cases discharged untreated (Outcome D2) and CDI prevalence at discharge (Outcome B3) are mostly false negatives at this level of testing (missed cases `r etri("cum_total_missed_cases")`). At `r prob(lo_sent)` they respond much less (`r etri("cum_total_missed_cases", lo_sent)`), as most CDI cases are never tested and missed whatever the test sensitivity.
  - Faecal specimens tested per confirmed case (Outcome C6) is `r e2(el("tests_per_confirmed", P1))` under every policy and daily probability of testing, as it equals 1 / sensitivity.
- **Less than in proportion (0.1 to 1)**: `r el_group("responsive")`.
  - The mean time from symptom onset to treatment (Outcome D6) is `r etri("mean_wait_treatment")` at `r prob(hi_sent)`, and `r etri("mean_wait_treatment", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`: the delay from false negative results and retests saved by better sensitivity is the same in days (see Outcome D6 in section [16) Commentary on the effect of improving test sensitivity]), but makes up a larger share of the shorter time to treatment when cases are sent for testing sooner.
  - Faecal specimens tested (Outcome C5, `r etri("cum_total_test")`) and CDI-attributable deaths (Outcome D4, `r etri("cum_deaths_CDI_attributable")`) fall by less than in proportion.
  - Confirmed cases (Outcome A5) rise by less than in proportion (`r etri("cum_confirmed_cases")`). The elasticity of the proportion of incident cases confirmed is the same at `r prob(lo_sent)` and `r prob(hi_sent)` (`r e2(el("prop_confirmed", P1, lo_sent))` and `r e2(el("prop_confirmed", P1, hi_sent))` under P1), as sensitivity changes the chance of confirmation for the cases tested, not the share of cases tested.
  - Hospital-acquired colonisations (Outcome B1) and CDI cases (Outcome B2) are most responsive under `r el_order("cum_hospital_attributable_I")` (`r etri("cum_hospital_attributable_I")` at `r prob(hi_sent)`; `r etri("cum_hospital_attributable_I", lo_sent)` at `r prob(lo_sent)`).
  - Side-room bed-days (Outcome C3) rise with the confirmed cases isolated (P2 `r e2(el("side_room_bed_days", P2))`, P3 `r e2(el("side_room_bed_days", P3))`; none under P1).
- **Barely responsive (below 0.1)**: `r el_group("barely")`. Sensitivity does not change who is sent for testing, so the share of incident cases ever sent for testing (Outcome A3) and the mean time to first test (Outcome D5) do not change at all. Incident CDI cases (Outcome A1, `r etri("cum_total_infected_incidence")`) change much less than hospital-acquired CDI, as cases admitted with CDI or colonised on admission are not affected, and bed-days and length of stay barely change.

Most outcomes are more responsive the more cases are sent for testing. At `r prob(lo_sent)`, the outcomes that respond more than in proportion are: `r el_group("elastic", lo_sent)`; and those that barely respond: `r el_group("barely", lo_sent)`.

## End of script
